# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** 19 years old  <sub>[v4 c3 P7](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c3 P5](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0005), [v4 c17 P27](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0027)</sub>
- **Origin:** United States  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- **Role:** Student and poet  <sub>[v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033), [v4 c17 P27](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0027)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Master Paul  <sub>[v2 c19 P22](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0022)</sub>

## Appearance

As a boy, Paul was small for his age, with delicate and refined facial features framed by a halo of chestnut curls, and big, meditative dark blue eyes. As he grew up, his hair was cut into close-cropped brown locks, and by age nineteen he had developed into a tall, splendid six-foot young man.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)_

## Personality

Paul is a deeply imaginative, sensitive, and grave boy whose inner spirit often seems older than his age. He possesses a vivid imagination filled with dream-people and poetic fancies, though he remains polite, fair-minded, and manly in his daily life. Highly perceptive and thoughtful, he holds deep affection and loyalty toward those he loves.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c11 P41](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0041), [v2 c15 P1](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0001), [v2 c19 P23](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0023), [v2 c19 P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033), [v2 c23 P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), [v2 c27 P54](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0054), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006)_

## History

After his mother passed away, Paul Irving came from the United States to live with his grandmother in Avonlea, attending the local school under Anne Shirley. He and Anne instantly formed a close bond as kindred spirits, and he became her favorite pupil. During his time at school, he befriended his teacher, introduced her to his rich imaginative world, and occasionally visited Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. When his father, Stephen Irving, came to visit Avonlea, Paul unwittingly helped reunite his father with Miss Lavendar, leading to their marriage. Following the wedding, Paul moved to Boston to live with his father and stepmother, while continuing to visit Echo Lodge in Prince Edward Island during summer vacations. As he grew older, he outgrew his imaginary childhood playmates and turned his attention to sports and writing. His poetry began to be accepted by magazines, earning praise from Anne. At nineteen, he returned to Avonlea to attend Anne's wedding before departing for two years of study abroad.

## Quotes

> Please, teacher, I found these in Mr. Wright’s field, and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . . I like you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> I never got really acquainted with him until after my little mother died. But he’s splendid when you do get to know him. I love him the best in all the world, and Grandma Irving next, and then you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009)</sub>

> Mrs. Lynde, father made a pretty good job of picking out my first mother and I could trust him to pick out just as good a one the second time.  <sub>[v2 c19 P22](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0022)</sub>

> I knew I could trust father to pick me out a nice little second mother. It’s a fine thing to have a father you can depend on, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c29 P2](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0002)</sub>

> You’ll never grow old, Teacher. You are one of the fortunate mortals who have found and drunk from the Fountain of Youth,—you and Mother Lavendar. See here! When you’re married I WON’T call you Mrs. Blythe. To me you’ll always be 'Teacher’—the teacher of the best lessons I ever learned.  <sub>[v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>
